items.problem: External MSBuild Include+Link items were invisible to bootstrap, forcing lossy manual reconstruction.
items.evidence: D1; turn 2 copied 10 files while Store.csproj declared 19 additional supported linked files.
items.change: Materialize resolvable linked Compile/ApplicationDefinition/Page/Content files at safe Link paths before rewrite and triage; report unresolved links.
items.expected_effect: Shared App/MainPage/styles/pages/assets enter the migration mapping at their correct logical paths without manual copying.
items.hierarchy_rationale: Tier 1 is feasible and deterministic; a template cannot predict arbitrary legacy Link graphs, and prose would remain skippable.
items.devils_advocate: The parser intentionally handles only supported linked files, skips legacy AssemblyInfo.cs, rejects unsafe Link paths, and reports unresolved properties rather than inventing locations.
items.falsifiable_check: Running bootstrap on Store reports 19 externally linked files, zero unresolved, and creates Styles/Styles.xaml plus App/MainPage linked files.

items.problem: Validator missed broken local merged-dictionary paths and disagreed with bootstrap's no-defer sentinel.
items.evidence: D3 and D6; final App.xaml points to absent /Styles/Styles.xaml, and turns 36/39/46 show the false no-defer warning.
items.root_cause: Validator checked manifest images but not local XAML dictionary paths, and its sentinel parser did not accept the producer's `(none)` row.
items.change: Fail on missing local ResourceDictionary Source files with file/line diagnostics; accept the bootstrap no-items row.
items.expected_effect: A deterministic pre-launch failure names the resource path instead of a generic 0xc000027b; zero-defer migrations are warning-free.
items.hierarchy_rationale: Tier 1 directly observes package-path invariants; adding startup-crash prose would still leave agents guessing.
items.devils_advocate: The check ignores explicit URI schemes and assembly-component resources to avoid rejecting framework/package dictionaries.
items.falsifiable_check: A fixture with Source=/Styles/Missing.xaml fails at App.xaml:1; a fixture with the `(none)` defer row passes consistency.

items.problem: Build guidance used a nonexistent command, missed default dotnet output, and did not cover recurring SDK default-item or implicit-using collisions.
items.evidence: D2, D4, D5, and G1; turn 24 rejected winapp build, turn 25 hit NETSDK1022, turn 27 hit CS0104 for System.Net.Http versus Windows.Web.Http, and turn 33 missed bin/Debug after a successful build.
items.root_cause: Instructions and launch tooling assumed obsolete/platform-qualified workflows, while common SDK-style project defaults were absent or too narrowly explained.
items.change: Use native dotnet build consistently, make Test-AppLaunch search bin/Debug as well as platform-qualified paths, document that local XAML Page items are implicit by default, and generalize CS0104 guidance to retained Windows projections colliding with SDK implicit usings.
items.expected_effect: The documented build command exists, its normal output is immediately consumable by launch diagnostics, and agents can resolve the first SDK-style build failures without trial-and-error project rewrites.
items.hierarchy_rationale: Layout discovery is Tier 1; the minimal Tier 3 edits are required for compiler diagnostics whose correct fix depends on project intent and type semantics rather than a safe automatic rewrite.
items.devils_advocate: Platform-qualified paths remain first; explicit Page management remains supported when default items are deliberately disabled; CS0104 guidance requires choosing the intended API rather than blindly removing namespaces.
items.falsifiable_check: No `winapp build` remains in migration guidance, a bin/Debug fixture is discovered, and the common-errors section maps NETSDK1022 plus non-XAML CS0104 collisions to deterministic fixes.
